translations.text: Blessed is God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort.
Not that we rule over your faith, but we are fellow workers for your joy, for you stand firm in faith.
But if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me, but, to some extent—not to put too much of a burden on you—all of you.
Among them, the god of this age has blinded the hearts of the unbelievers so that they cannot see the light of the good news of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
We know that the one who raised Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and bring us to stand together with you.
Therefore we strive to please him, whether we are in the body or outside it.
So from now on we know no one according to the flesh. Even if we once knew Christ according to the flesh, we no longer know him that way.
What agreement is there between Christ and Beliar? What share does a believer have with an unbeliever?

Look at what this sorrow in accordance with God has produced in you: great earnestness, a defense of yourselves, distress, fear, love, zeal, and punishment. In every respect you have shown yourselves to be pure in this matter.
As it is written, “The one who had much did not have too much, and the one who had little did not have too little.”
For he accepted our appeal, but, being even more eager, he set out to come to you of his own accord.
We are guarding ourselves in this, so that no one may blame us concerning this substantial gift that we are administering.

On frequent journeys, in dangers from rivers, in dangers from robbers, in dangers from my own people, in dangers from the Gentiles, in dangers in the city, in dangers in the wilderness, in dangers at sea, in dangers among false brothers.
He was caught up into paradise and heard hidden words that a person is not permitted to speak.
That is why I write these things while I am not with you, so that when I come I will not have to act harshly, according to the authority the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.
